subject.title: feat(linux): Quick Chat agent switcher, avatars, per-agent routing, and configurable shortcut

question: Should the Linux companion be allowed to load arbitrary HTTP(S) avatar images from agent identity/configuration, including through an application-level `img-src` CSP expansion?
rationale: This is a product trust and privacy boundary: a mechanical implementation can preserve local/data avatars, but only maintainers can decide whether remote avatar egress is intended for the companion and whether it may apply to all companion webviews.

options.title: Keep local/data-only avatars
options.body: Retain the current restrictive CSP and have Linux Quick Chat fall back to emoji or monogram when an avatar is remote.

options.title: Approve scoped remote avatars
options.body: Allow remote avatar loading only with a narrowly scoped companion policy, explicit privacy documentation, and tests covering allowed and denied URL sources.

options.title: Defer remote avatar support
options.body: Land the switcher and shortcut work only after separating remote avatar rendering into a follow-up with an agreed security contract.

recommendation.title: Keep local/data-only avatars
recommendation.body: Retain the current restrictive CSP and have Linux Quick Chat fall back to emoji or monogram when an avatar is remote.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the Linux Quick Chat foundation and authored the current companion, agent-summary, and CSP changes.
